title: How the app reads from and writes to SQLite (the 6 query modules)
purpose: Show the read/write boundary between the app and the database. Every SQL statement in Surf lives inside one of 6 small modules — one per table family. The teacher should see that no random script ever writes a SQL string directly; everything goes through these named helpers. Phase 2 pages will only call functions in this layer.
audience: non-engineer teammates and the grading teacher

groups.label: DB infra — opens the connection, applies the schema
Query modules (one per table family) — every read and write goes through these
SQLite tables (8) — see db_structure_v1 for the full schema
Phase 1 callers — who uses the query layer today

nodes.label: connection.connect
nodes.description: Opens a sqlite3 connection at ~/.surf/user.sqlite, runs the schema.sql file (idempotent CREATE IF NOT EXISTS), enables foreign keys

nodes.label: schema/schema.sql (single-file DDL, D-3.1 wipe-and-rerun)
nodes.description: All 8 tables + 10 indexes in one file. To apply schema changes during the build: delete the .sqlite file and re-run

nodes.label: queries_classes
nodes.description: insert_class, get_class_by_id, list_classes_for_user. Encodes/decodes factsheet_json transparently

nodes.label: lecture_ingest.ingest_lecture
nodes.description: Phase 1's main caller — uses 5 of the 6 query modules during ingestion

nodes.label: factsheet_clean (cleaner + renderer)
nodes.description: Writes through queries_classes when a class is created; renderer reads back through it

nodes.label: Phase 2+ pages will be added here as they ship
nodes.description: Mock-take, dashboard, settings pages will all call this same query layer — diagram will be updated end of Phase 2
